title: 3Sum
description: Given an integer array nums, return all the triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j, i != k, and j != k, and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.
reason: The optimal solution sorts the array and then uses a two‑pointer scan for each fixed element to find complementary pairs that sum to zero.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without duplicate characters.
reason: Uses a moving window with two pointers to maintain a substring and a hash set/map to detect duplicates efficiently.

title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Given two strings s and t, return the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t, including duplicates, is included in the window.
reason: The solution expands and contracts a window over the string using two pointers while maintaining character counts in a hash map to satisfy the requirement.

title: Permutation in String
description: Given two strings s1 and s2, return true if s2 contains a permutation of s1, or false otherwise.
reason: The solution maintains a fixed-size window over s2 and updates character frequency counts (hash table) while moving two pointers to check for a permutation of s1.

title: Container With Most Water
description: Given an integer array height, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container that contains the most water.
reason: The optimal solution uses two pointers at both ends of the array and moves the pointer with the smaller height inward, a greedy choice that maximizes area in linear time.

title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
description: Given a 1-indexed array of integers that is already sorted in non-decreasing order, find two numbers such that they add up to a specific target number.
reason: The sorted nature of the input allows a linear two‑pointer scan to find the pair in O(n). An alternative is to fix one element and binary‑search for its complement, linking the binary search pattern as a secondary approach.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
description: Given a string s and an integer k, return the length of the longest substring containing the same letter you can get after replacing at most k characters.
reason: The solution maintains a dynamic window over the string, expanding and shrinking it while tracking character frequencies with a hash map to ensure at most k replacements.

title: Fruit Into Baskets
description: You are visiting a farm with a row of fruit trees. You have two baskets and each basket can hold only one type of fruit. Find the maximum number of fruits you can collect.
reason: The problem asks for the longest contiguous subarray containing at most two distinct fruit types, which is solved by expanding and shrinking a window while tracking counts using a hash map.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description: Given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a stock on the ith day, maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy one stock and a different day to sell that stock.
reason: Iterate once, keep the smallest price seen so far and compute profit with the current price, updating the maximum profit – a classic greedy/ prefix‑min approach.

title: Contains Duplicate II
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return true if there are two distinct indices i and j such that nums[i] == nums[j] and abs(i - j) <= k.
reason: Maintain a window of the last k elements using a hash set to detect a duplicate within distance k in O(n) time.

title: Network Delay Time
description: You are given a network of n nodes and directed edges with travel times. Find how long it takes for all nodes to receive a signal sent from a given node.
reason: The problem requires finding the minimum travel time from a source node to all other nodes in a weighted directed graph, which is solved efficiently with Dijkstra's algorithm using a min‑heap.

title: Path With Minimum Effort
description: You are given a heights matrix where heights[row][col] represents the height of a cell. Find a path from the top-left to the bottom-right that minimizes the maximum absolute difference in heights between consecutive cells.
reason: The problem asks for minimizing the maximum edge weight along a path, which can be solved by binary searching the effort threshold and checking reachability via BFS/DFS, or directly by a Dijkstra‑style minimax path using a priority queue.

title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
description: There are n cities connected by flights. Find the cheapest price from a source city to a destination city with at most k stops.
reason: The problem asks for the minimum‑cost path with at most K edges, which is a classic constrained shortest‑path problem solved by DP over the number of stops (Bellman‑Ford) or by a state‑expanded Dijkstra using a heap.

title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
description: Given an n x n binary matrix, return the shortest clear path from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell. A clear path consists only of cells containing 0.
reason: The problem asks for the minimum number of steps from start to end in a binary matrix, which is naturally modeled as an unweighted graph where each cell is a node and edges exist between 8-directionally adjacent clear cells. BFS guarantees the shortest path in such graphs.

title: Number of Islands
description: Given an m x n 2D binary grid, count the number of islands. An island is surrounded by water and is formed by connecting adjacent land cells horizontally or vertically.
reason: The problem reduces to finding connected components in a 2D grid, which is typically solved by graph traversal (DFS/BFS) or Union‑Find; the grid representation adds the matrix pattern.

title: Rotting Oranges
description: Given a grid where each cell contains a fresh orange, rotten orange, or empty cell, return the minimum number of minutes until no fresh orange remains.
reason: The problem spreads rot from all initially rotten oranges simultaneously, which is modeled as a multi-source BFS on a 2D grid, processing cells level by level to compute the minimum minutes.

title: Is Graph Bipartite?
description: Given an undirected graph, return true if and only if it is bipartite.
reason: The task is to explore each component of an undirected graph and assign one of two colors to vertices, ensuring no edge connects same‑colored vertices. BFS or DFS with a two‑color scheme is the core technique, while Union‑Find or component analysis can serve as alternative approaches.

title: Climbing Stairs
description: You are climbing a staircase. It takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can climb either one or two steps. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.
reason: The problem reduces to counting ways to reach step n, which follows the Fibonacci recurrence f(n)=f(n-1)+f(n-2). It can be solved via DP (bottom‑up or top‑down with memoization) or simple recursion.

title: House Robber
description: Given an array of integers representing money in houses, determine the maximum amount of money you can rob without robbing two adjacent houses.
reason: The solution builds a DP array where each state depends only on the previous two states, allowing O(n) time and O(1) extra space by compressing the state.

title: Binary Search
description: Given an array of integers nums sorted in ascending order and a target value, return the index of target if it exists in nums, otherwise return -1.
reason: The solution repeatedly halves the search interval on a sorted array, which is the classic binary search technique, a divide‑and‑conquer approach.
